entries.title: Satellite index against EA visual algae checks
entries.verdict: Failed as stated. For "algae seen" the index's AUC was 0.604 (97.5% interval 0.394 to 0.746) against a bar of 0.65; adding it to month and the last check made the Brier score worse (−0.00465, interval −0.02282 to +0.00203). Only 404 of 1,358 checks had a usable image within 3 days. "Objectionable" algae had only 20 events: too few to judge.
entries.scope: 14 of 18 English lake bathing waters on 8 water bodies, EA visual checks May to September 2020-21 and 2023-26. Small ponds had no core water pixels.
entries.stage_note: This classifier is archived. Its image extraction and coverage work is reused by the satellite observations now shown on the Lakes page.
entries.reopen_when: A different, better-measured target (for example lab chlorophyll or verified bloom reports) with enough clear images, or a method that reads small ponds. Not a rerun of the same visual classifier.

records.quote: **Verdicts: A (algae seen) fails. B (objectionable) is too few to judge.**
| 1. AUC of the raw reading ≥ 0.65, lower end > 0.50 | 0.604 (0.394 to 0.746) | no |

entries.register_note: The register gives the interval without saying it is a 97.5% interval, and does not mention that the within-lake placebo check passed for both outcomes.

entries.title: Satellite index against lab chlorophyll
entries.verdict: Failed as stated, by 0.0003 on one condition: the pooled Spearman correlation was 0.502 with a 95% interval of 0.2997 to 0.667, and the lower end had to be above 0.3. It beat the within-lake placebo. Overall calibration skill 0.159 (−0.058 to 0.325), too uncertain. Classified afterwards (#407) as "promising, not validated"; the verdict itself was not changed.
entries.scope: 207 pairs at 38 English lake sampling points, May to September 2021 and 2023-26, satellite image within a day of the lab sample. Shallow lakes 0.301 (0.052 to 0.475), but that subgroup was singled out after the result was seen.
entries.stage_note: Dated index readings are shown as observations on the Lakes page, with a weekly pilot at five sites since 31 October 2026. They are not converted to chlorophyll, an algae warning or swimming advice.
entries.next: Review the draft 2027 shallow-lake protocol before 1 May 2027, then collect new readings weekly from 1 May 2027 for a fair test.

records.quote: | 1. Pooled Spearman ≥ 0.5, interval lower end > 0.3 | ρ = 0.502, 95% interval **0.2997** to 0.667 | **no, by 0.0003 on the lower end** |
**Verdict unchanged: fails as stated. Classification: promising, not validated.**

entries.register_note: The register says the shallow subset "was selected after results". The shallow/deeper split was written into the test before the run; what came after the result was treating the shallow subset as the lead finding.

entries.title: Satellite index against harmful-algae incidents
entries.verdict: Too few to judge. The test needed incidents at 4 or more water bodies; there were 3. As description only: a stratified score of 0.64 (95% interval 0.33 to 0.73), which did not beat a seasonal-shift placebo; season-adjusted about 0.48.
entries.scope: 14 lake bathing waters on 8 water bodies, EA harmful-algae incidents May to September 2020-26 (2022 has no images).
entries.stage_note: Archived as a model. Official harmful-algae notices stay on the site as their own observed record, separate from satellite readings.
entries.reopen_when: Better incident collection gives incidents at 4 or more water bodies with matched images, with an independent check.

records.quote: **Verdict: too few to judge.**
- **Primary (description):** stratified S = 0.64, 95% interval 0.33 to 0.73, label "Too uncertain".

entries.register_note: The register lists the figures without the verdict word or the doc's statement that they are description only and decide nothing. "Matched imagery at only 3 waterbodies" is loose: 13 incidents were found, 9 with a reading on an incident day, at 3 water bodies.

entries.title: Spill model trained on all nine water companies
entries.verdict: Not adopted, twice. Version 1 failed 3 of 4 conditions. Version 2's offset arm was 11 to 23% better at eight companies (pooled Brier gain −0.00550, interval −0.00883 to −0.00268) but 3.4% worse at United Utilities (+0.00007 to +0.00261), so it failed the "no company clearly worse" condition. The other arm failed at United Utilities too (+9.0%).
entries.scope: EA start/stop files for nine English companies, trained 2024-25, tested January to August 2026.
entries.stage_note: A routing rule (version 2 at the eight companies, today's model at United Utilities and everywhere else) is logged in shadow beside the live forecast. It does not change any spot's level.
entries.next: Read the shadow window (31 October to 27 November 2026) on 28 November 2026.

entries.title: Lake water temperature model
entries.verdict: Failed: four of six conditions failed, and it was worse for large and deep lakes (bias −0.40 °C, mean absolute error 1.44 °C). A separate check on a historical buoy at Blelham Tarn (0.5 m) gave 1.38 °C against 1.77 °C for 7-day air; at Windermere the benefit disappeared when both basins were left out of training.
entries.scope: 220 held-out English lake waters, May to September 2026, EA spot samples. The buoy check is one small lake, 2016-19, with no intervals.
entries.stage_note: Past EA lake temperature measurements are shown on the Measured lake temperatures page, never as today's temperature.

entries.verdict: Both questions failed. The dry-spell term itself failed three conditions and pointed the opposite way to the idea (gain −0.00024, interval −0.00136 to +0.00080). 72-hour rain gained +0.00049 against a 0.0005 margin, interval including zero.
entries.scope: The E. coli model's EA samples; a longer rain window helped rivers a little, not enough to clear the bar.
